content:
Dear Quillstone Payments Hiring Team,

I am applying for the Machine Learning Engineer – Customer Support AI role. My experience developing and operating NLP systems for Croatian administrative and customer-support text aligns closely with your team’s work on models that route tickets and help support agents.

At Slavonica Document AI, I built and deployed a document classifier covering 23 classes, achieving 94% accuracy and a macro F1 of 0.91. The FastAPI service runs in Docker on Azure App Service and processes approximately 15,000 documents per day. I have also developed a Croatian named entity recognition model and implemented weekly monitoring reports. When monitoring revealed an OCR change that had reduced model accuracy by nine percentage points, the issue was addressed within a week. This work has given me practical experience with model serving, monitoring, Azure, Python, and MLflow.

Earlier, at Baranjska kreditna banka, I worked on customer churn prediction and complaint classification, including a classifier for 11 complaint topics used in weekly reporting to customer service management. I have also built a personal weekend prototype for question answering over Croatian laws using retrieval-augmented generation. My RAG experience is at the prototype stage; my production experience is in classification, NER, serving, and monitoring. I am currently pursuing doctoral research on named entity recognition in Croatian legal texts, expected to conclude in 2027.

I am drawn to the opportunity to build practical AI systems for customer operations and to Quillstone’s emphasis on ownership, teamwork, and learning from mistakes. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my experience in NLP and production document AI could contribute to your team.

Kind regards,
Petra Zlatarić-Novosel

critique.content_quality_feedback: The cover letter is concise, professional, truthful, and well structured. It uses relevant evidence rather than unsupported claims, including the 23-class classifier, 94% accuracy, 0.91 macro F1, 15,000 documents per day, model monitoring, and the nine-percentage-point accuracy impact. It also handles the limited RAG experience appropriately by clearly identifying it as a personal prototype rather than implying production LLM experience. The main content weakness is that it omits some of the strongest supporting evidence from the candidate material, especially the 4,000-document annotated dataset, inter-annotator kappa of 0.87, Azure ML, and the specific customer-support relevance of the complaint-classification work. The letter also does not clearly distinguish the candidate's production experience from the job's four-year requirement.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The plain-text formatting, standard paragraph structure, conventional greeting, and absence of tables, graphics, or unusual formatting are ATS-friendly. Important keywords such as machine learning, NLP, classification, NER, Python, FastAPI, Docker, Azure, MLflow, model serving, and monitoring are present. AI screening probability is moderate to good for NLP, Azure, model serving, and monitoring criteria, but weaker for the exact terms 'data versioning,' 'feature engineering,' 'data ingestion pipelines,' 'MLOps,' and 'production software engineering.' The letter should not add unsupported terms, but it can use 'MLOps' where the existing MLflow, serving, and monitoring evidence supports that characterization. A cover letter is supplementary to the CV, so its ATS value is limited; nevertheless, explicitly naming the strongest supported technologies would improve keyword matching.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The document aligns well with the role's NLP, text classification, model serving, monitoring, Azure, Python, MLflow, and customer-support-related work. The complaint-topic classifier and the RAG prototype are relevant to support AI, while the transparent description of the RAG project demonstrates credibility. The candidate's material shows gaps against several stated requirements: no completed degree is provided; the material does not establish at least four years of shipping ML or AI systems to production; production data versioning is not evidenced; and feature engineering and data-ingestion pipeline experience are not evidenced. These are candidate-profile gaps rather than cover-letter wording defects. The letter could nevertheless make the existing production evidence and customer-operations relevance more explicit. The culture paragraph is appropriately grounded in the advertisement's ownership, teamwork, and learning-from-mistakes themes without inventing personal claims.
critique.improvement_instructions:
CRITICAL: In the paragraph beginning 'At Slavonica Document AI,' add the strongest available data-quality evidence after the NER sentence: 'For the NER work, I created annotation guidelines and a 4,000-document dataset with two annotators, achieving an inter-annotator kappa of 0.87.' This directly demonstrates preparation and evaluation of large text datasets and strengthens the connection to production AI development.

CRITICAL: In the same Slavonica paragraph, change 'This work has given me practical experience with model serving, monitoring, Azure, Python, and MLflow' to 'This work has given me practical MLOps experience with Python, model serving, monitoring, Azure ML, Azure App Service, Docker, and MLflow.' Use this wording only because the CV and candidate portfolio document all of these technologies and activities.

MINOR: In the paragraph about Baranjska kreditna banka, make the customer-support application more explicit by changing 'a classifier for 11 complaint topics used in weekly reporting to customer service management' to 'a customer-complaint classifier for 11 topics, used in weekly reporting to customer service management.' This more closely matches the role's customer-support AI terminology without overstating the system as a conversational assistant.

MINOR: In the final paragraph, replace 'practical AI systems for customer operations' with 'production AI systems for customer operations' only if the preceding production examples remain in the letter. This will connect the candidate's documented Azure deployment and monitoring work more directly to the responsibility to build, deploy, and operate AI systems.
